nodes.title: Declare value as a model
nodes.why: model(0) registers a value input and a valueChange output in one field, the exact pair [(value)] binds to, and inside the child it reads and writes like a signal.
nodes.alternative: Pair @Input() value with @Output() valueChange = new EventEmitter<number>(), or input() with output(), and emit the next value by hand.
nodes.tradeoff: One field replaces two declarations, but the child now holds a copy of the value; the stateless input() plus output() pair never shows a number the parent has not accepted.

nodes.title: Write the model instead of emitting
nodes.why: update changes the child's value and emits valueChange with the result in one call, so the plus button needs no EventEmitter and the parent's [(value)] receives the new number.
nodes.alternative: Emit this.value + 1 from an output and show the new number only after the parent sends it back through [value].
nodes.tradeoff: The child shows the new number at once; a parent that bound only [value] and ignored valueChange would see the child drift away from its own value.

nodes.title: Keep the value at zero or above
nodes.why: The minus button is disabled at 0, and Math.max holds the floor if dec() runs at 0 some other way; a model set to its current value emits nothing, so no extra valueChange goes out.
nodes.alternative: Rely on [disabled]="value() === 0" alone, or let the value go negative and reject it in the parent.
nodes.tradeoff: The clamp repeats a rule the disabled button already enforces, but it keeps dec() correct for a keyboard shortcut or a test that calls it directly.

nodes.title: Flip the like flag through its model
nodes.why: update stores the negation of the current liked value and the model emits likedChange, so the parent's liked signal and its true or false stat follow the click.
nodes.alternative: Keep liked as plain child state that the parent never hears about, or emit !this.liked from an output for the parent to assign.
nodes.tradeoff: The flag now lives in two places, the child's model and the parent's signal, kept equal by [(liked)]; a child-only flag is simpler but invisible to the stats row.

nodes.title: Keep the source of truth in parent signals
nodes.why: The parent's value and liked signals are what [(value)]="value" and [(liked)]="liked" read and write: Angular calls set on them when the child emits, and the stats row reads value() and liked().
nodes.alternative: Plain value and liked fields, which [(value)] also accepts but which an OnPush parent would not re-render if they changed outside its template.
nodes.tradeoff: The binding passes the signal without parentheses while the interpolation calls it, a split that is easy to get wrong; in return every change is tracked.
